text: A European small company was developing onboard equipment that lets an aircraft, piloted or remotely operated, work out its own heading, altitude and position when satellite positioning drops out, built without any US-supplied parts or technical data so that American export controls would not restrict its sale. Which French firm's competing product did it single out as the existing rival that was already free of those export controls?
reference_answer: NICENAV (Civitanavi Systems) named Sagem, a French company, as the competitor already offering an ITAR-free INS solution for high-performance airborne applications, one that was likewise DO-178C and DO-254 certified. NICENAV positioned its own system as costing about 20% less and as being built on FOG technology rather than the RLG technology behind the Sagem product.
notes: Seed 682337 (NICENAV, SME-1 feasibility study, Civitanavi Systems) taken from corpus_profile cp6 candidate vector-31; drift check re-ran the candidate SQL (social geography path x objective LIKE '%inertial navigation%') and still returns exactly 682337. Question composed after reading the seed's objective and report; the answering fact is the 'Competition:' passage of the objective naming Sagem. The nationality clause ('Which French firm's competing product') is drawn from that same sentence and is the disambiguator: it rules out Honeywell, the US ITAR-COMPLIANT incumbent named in 682337's own report summary and in 738851's objective, by the question text rather than by a negative qualifier alone. Pooled adjudication on the final wording (k=10, 23 pooled projects): 682337 IN - objective names Sagem (French company) as the ITAR-free rival; its best chunk in the pool is that objective. OUT: 738851 (NICENAV phase 2, same company/product - names Honeywell's LASEREF VI as the dominant rival but describes it as US, RLG-based and ITAR-COMPLIANT, and names no French firm and no firm already free of the export controls); 855443 DACTREOC, 761964 OrbEx, 859474 PRIME, 817378 EXOTRAIL, 827490 AMPSS, 685963 ALTAIR (satellite attitude control, micro-launchers, space propulsion - not aircraft navigation equipment); 870365 MORAL, 854520 3H-ADC (export-restriction-free space electronics, not aircraft navigation, no named rival firm); 775495 MAGYCO, 699387 NAVISAS, 698729 GLAD-2, 650877 AST-FCS_vF, 878318 TOM-E (aviation/positioning or flight-control products but no export-control framing and no named competing firm); 890599 SAFELAND, 894593 ICARUS, 882831 COOLSOE, 762392 YawSTOP, 726904 OnceForAll, 741467 FIRMNET, 726168 GLOBALMACRO, 827760 Bob (off-topic: ATM, altitude reference, cooling, cargo stabilisation, business software, economics, home appliances). Completeness sweep via run_sql, non-embedding, unchanged by the edit because the added clause only narrows the question: (a) objective LIKE '%SAGEM%' OR '% ITAR%' OR '%ITAR-%' OR '%(ITAR%' -> 10 projects, only 682337 and 738851 in the aircraft-navigation domain (others: Space-COTS, OpenDreamKit, S3NET, PALACE, SENSORIANCE, PIONEERS, 3H-ADC, MORAL); SENSORIANCE 785315 read in full - ITAR-free aircraft VISION system, no positioning function and no named rival - OUT. (b) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser LIKE '%SAGEM%' OR '%ITAR-FREE%' OR '%ITAR FREE%' OR '%ITAR REGULATION%' OR '%ITAR COMPLIAN%' -> 17 projects; only 682337 and 738851 are airborne navigation equipment, the rest being propulsion (Rheform), rad-hard electronics (VEGAS, OPERA, EFESOS, HERMES, DUROC, 3H-ADC, MORAL), radar (GRACE), aileron actuation (TAIRA), and unrelated software/mining projects. Gold therefore stays at 1 -> L1. term_style=paraphrase: the question avoids every distinctive technical term the seed uses (ITAR, fibre optic gyroscope/FOG, RLG, inertial navigation system/INS, DO-178C/DO-254, navigation-grade). It does now share the ordinary word 'French' with the gold sentence, and the rank matrix after the edit is lexical 2 / dense 5 / hybrid 5 / hybrid_rerank 2 - lexical-first, which is weaker support for a paraphrase label than the pre-edit matrix (dense absent, lexical 6); recorded as a WARN rather than relabelled, since the cell is fixed at paraphrase.

text: How do metabolites produced by the gut microbiota after bariatric surgery affect the host, according to EU-funded research?
reference_answer: Two projects trace a metabolite of the post-surgery gut microbiota to an effect on the host. EnteroBariatric reports that Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) shifts the microbiome from Firmicutes to the Proteobacteria phylum and raises faecal Enterobacteriaceae, and that metabolites of the RYGB-associated microbiota - notably tyramine, which can come directly from diet or be produced by intestinal Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae - promote colon cancer risk via increased DNA damage, cell proliferation and inflammation. Drug the bug runs the other way: the surgery-altered microbiota produces less imidazole propionate, a histidine-derived metabolite made by the microbial enzyme UrdA (urocanate reductase) that is elevated in prediabetes and type 2 diabetes and induces insulin resistance, so the project synthesized and screened more than 40 compounds seeking inhibitors of that enzyme as a new class of diabetes medication. In both, a molecule produced by the post-surgery gut microbiota is the proposed mediator of a host outcome: in Drug the bug the altered microbiota may be directly linked to some of the metabolic improvements observed following surgery, with imidazole propionate reduced after surgery, while in EnteroBariatric metabolites produced by RYGB-associated gut microbiota modulate the colorectal cancer risk.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-66 (bariatric surgery cluster, 4 projects corpus-wide); drift check re-ran the candidate SQL and reproduced 704779, 715662, 780659, 803526 exactly. The candidate's claim that all four use the operation as a mechanistic lever did NOT survive reading: 704779 Fit-The-Fat mentions bariatric surgery only as background to motivate non-invasive alternatives and studies visceral-adipose-tissue T cells instead. A broader first wording ('what molecular mechanisms have projects identified by studying what changes after bariatric surgery') pooled 5 satisfying projects (715662, 780659, 803526, 695069, 694717) = L3, so the question was tightened to the microbiota-metabolite thread, which is where the two gold projects share a genuine common finding. Adjudications - IN: 715662 EnteroBariatric (RYGB-associated microbiota metabolites, tyramine, colon cancer risk), 780659 Drug the bug (imidazole propionate reduced after surgery, UrdA inhibitors). OUT: 803526 BARINAFLD (hybrid rank 7 - weight-loss-independent hepatic mechanisms, Egr1 and one-carbon/choline metabolism; no microbial metabolite); 695069 BYPASSWITHOUTSURGERY (gut hormone GLP-1 hypersecretion from host enteroendocrine cells, not microbial metabolites); 694717 ImmunoBile (bile acids and FXR/TGR5 immune signalling; its post-RYGB measurement is systemic total and conjugated bile-acid concentrations, host-conjugated, and it never links bacterial metabolite production to the surgery); 704779 Fit-The-Fat (VAT T cells, surgery only as background); 814638 GDS (non-surgical duodenal sleeve device, commercialization, no mechanism work); 633962 P4SB ('metabolic surgery' used metaphorically for engineering Pseudomonas putida); 796084 qMAR (antibiotic-resistance genes in paediatric transplant patients, not bariatric). All other pooled candidates (894369 SMs-Gut, 101002525 MoodBugs, 797267 Gut-AnorexiaNervosa, 101028971 AmmoniaVir, 801965 GUTSY, 635617 GAMES, 815962 Healthybiota, 890545 MicroILCs, 753893 MetaBiota, 101027450 BIOMA, 648084 CholangioConcept, 796838 BESIDE, 845036 Goc-MM, 708986 GallBiome, 794417 TRIANGLE, 797297 miVaO, 706353 MAIT, 752047 IMMUNO_CRC, 865568 GutBrainGABA) are gut-microbiota-metabolite projects with no bariatric-surgery component in their best chunk - OUT. Completeness sweep 1 (binding, since the question requires the surgery): objective/title ILIKE any of bariatric, gastric bypass, RYGB, sleeve gastrectomy, gastric banding, weight-loss surgery, weight loss surgery, metabolic surgery -> 8 projects (633962, 694717, 695069, 704779, 715662, 780659, 803526, 814638), all adjudicated above. Sweep 2: gastrectomy, duodenal switch, imidazole propionate, obesity surgery, after-surgery+microbio -> 780659 (gold) and 796084 (OUT). term_style exact-term: both gold texts use 'bariatric surgery', 'gut microbiota' and 'metabolite' verbatim, and both rank 1-2 under lexical. Reference-answer note (fix round): the closing synthesis sentence was rewritten to drop a weight-loss-independence contrast that only OUT project 803526 supports; it now carries 780659's own hedge ('may be directly linked to some of the metabolic improvements observed following surgery') and 715662's own verb ('modulate the colorectal cancer risk').

text: Which projects are engineering CAR T cells to attack solid tumours?
reference_answer: Eight H2020 projects engineer chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cells against solid tumours, the setting where CAR therapy has lagged behind its success in blood cancers. Several build new CAR specificities: AngioCAR aims CAR T cells at extracellular vimentin (eVim) on the tumour vasculature, SweetCAR at sialic-acid carbohydrate neoantigens on carcinomas, and CARsen at senescent cells in solid tumours and senescence-associated disease. Others attack the hostile tumour microenvironment instead - Exh-Res-CART and Tex-Mex both work on T-cell exhaustion (biochemical and biomechanical triggers respectively), TRAP-CART uses gene-modified blood-derived cells in the tumour microenvironment to switch on programmable CAR T cells locally, with melanoma as its model cancer, and EnhancemenT modulates ZFP36/ZFP36L1 RNA-binding proteins in CAR-T cells to raise their in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity. CARAT is the platform case: automated GMP-compliant manufacture of CAR-modified T cells together with innovative CAR designs, intended to serve patients with incurable solid tumours as well as haematologic malignancies.
notes: Seeds (read before the question existed): 839566 Exh-Res-CART, 893910 AngioCAR, 949667 CARsen, 957512 SweetCAR - all from the cp6 vector-17 CAR-T cluster. The candidate's own sample_ids 754658 CARAMBA and 733297 EURE-CART were read and adjudicated OUT (CARAMBA targets multiple myeloma, a haematologic malignancy; EURE-CART's stated trial is a first-in-man CAR T trial without a solid-tumour target), which is why the scope was narrowed from bare CAR-T to CAR T cells against solid tumours. Candidate drift check: the candidate's evidence SQL re-executed to n=12 unchanged. Pool adjudications (k=10, pooled union 18 projects, question text as recorded): IN 839566 (title/objective: exhaustion-resistant CAR-T for solid tumours), 893910 (develops CAR T cells against extracellular vimentin to target solid tumours), 949667 (senolytic CAR T cells for solid tumors), 667980 (designs innovative CARs and GMP manufacture of CAR-modified T cells 'serving patients with so far incurable solid tumours and hematologic malignancies'; report workPerformed: a partner 'develop[ed] novel CARs to target a solid tumo[ur]'), 101026676 (programmable CAR T cells for solid cancers, melanoma model), 101030034 (engineers synthetic biomechanosensor-actuator devices in T cells to remove 'a major obstacle in translating CAR T cell therapy to solid tumours'), 101022265 (will 'control the expression of these RBPs in CAR-T cells ... to enhance the in-vivo solid tumour-fighting capacity of these cells'). OUT: 805337 MechanoIMM (mechanical immunoengineering of adoptive T-cell therapy for solid tumours, but engineers no CAR), 786462 HOPE (NR2F6 checkpoint target; CAR-T for solid NSCLC named only as a direction it is 'considering'), 101001971 EPI-CART (CAR T epigenetics followed in patients with two blood cancers), 658490 CARiPSCTcells (off-the-shelf CAR T, multiple myeloma), 945393 T2EVOLVE (standards/access ecosystem for CAR and TCR therapy, no solid-tumour target), 721358 EN_ACTI2NG (CAR/TCR receptor biophysics, leukemia), 755402 STEPUP (synthetic dendritic cells for T-cell production, no CAR, no solid-tumour target), 877430 IMMUNOTRAP (diagnostic test for CAR-T toxicity), 101018587 ICoMICS (migration modelling and mechanically trained immune cells, no CAR), 893384 NANOCRISPR (CRISPR nanodelivery, prostate cancer), 794852 TCRabX (TCR affinity, not CAR). Completeness sweeps via run_sql, all hits adjudicated: (1) objective/title CAR terms corpus-wide = 34 projects; (2) CAR terms AND solid tumour/carcinoma/melanoma/glioblastoma/sarcoma in objective or title = 11 rows; (3) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults CAR terms AND 'solid tumo%' = 16 rows; (4) CAR terms AND 'solid cancer'/glioblastoma/pancreatic/breast/lung/ovarian = 9 rows. Sweep-only hits read and rejected: 796672 CellularNanoMachines (T cells as nanoparticle carriers), 804236 NextGen IO (hypoxia drug discovery), 805038 STIMUNO (tumour metabolite; CAR-T only as a therapy to test against), 823614 ONCOSMART (in-vitro diagnostics), 101025176 milieuPCa (single-cell omics of prostate cancer), 708169 BITCAT (oligonucleotide immunotherapeutics, glioblastoma), 765104 MATURE-NK (CAR-modified NK cells, not T cells), 707093 AVITAG (oncolytic alphavirus), 725051 EVOLVE (chimeric receptors on antigen-presenting cells, not T cells), 882918 TrojanDC (in-vivo dendritic-cell reprogramming; CAR-T mentioned only as a costly competitor), 948172 CrispSCNAs (copy-number biology), 850006 OCTAV (skin-cancer imaging). term_style exact-term: the question reuses 'CAR T cells' and 'solid tumours' verbatim from the gold texts (e.g. the Exh-Res-CART title 'Exhaustion-resistant CAR-T cells for the treatment of solid tumours'), and lexical ranked five gold members in its top-10 (839566 #1, 101030034 #4, 101022265 #7, 667980 #8, 949667 #9). Marginal members disclosed: 667980 CARAT (a manufacturing platform whose indication spans solid and haematologic disease), 101030034 Tex-Mex and 101022265 EnhancemenT (both modify the T cells used for CAR therapy against solid tumours rather than designing a new CAR). 957512 SweetCAR never writes 'solid tumour' - it contrasts its anti-carbohydrate CAR-T against carcinomas with current CAR-T that 'target mostly soluble tumors' - and it fell outside all four conditions' top-10 for the final wording (it was lexical #7 for an earlier near-identical wording).
